subject: Availability carveout & order-form path: workback and evidence request
messages:
From: Melissa Johnson <melissa.johnson@novacorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaCorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: 2025-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Availability carveout request + evidence for onboarding

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal and procurement are asking for a narrowly scoped availability carveout in the order form for an initial 6-month migration window where we will be running a mixture of batch and real-time inference. Specifically they want: 

- Clear definition of the scheduled maintenance window(s) and notification lead times.
- Historical uptime and 99th/95th latency percentiles for similar workloads (prod-like TPS and 8k token requests).
- Telemetry samples and a list of metrics you can commit to share during onboarding (token-level latency, queue depth, fail rate by status code).
- A simple credit schedule for availability breaches that is compatible with our procurement workflows.

Can you send a proposed workback and a short evidence checklist we can attach to the SOW/order form? Our preferred cadence is to close contract redlines by end of next week (7/25).

Also loop in whoever owns order-form language on your side so we can fast-track legal review.

Best,
Melissa Johnson
Director, Strategic Procurement
NovaCorp Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Melissa Johnson <melissa.johnson@novacorp.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2025-07-19T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability carveout request + evidence for onboarding

Melissa — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (sales ops) and Kimberly (enterprise legal) to help with order-form language and the credit schedule.

High-level proposed workback (can tighten if you need faster):
1) Today (7/19): We share an evidence checklist + draft redline for the order form (attached).
2) 7/20: Your legal/procurement reviews redlines, flags any hard stops.
3) 7/21: Redwood legal provides final redline and order-form language for Docusign routing.
4) 7/22-7/25: Execute signature and attach evidence pack to SOW.

Evidence checklist (attached: Telemetry-Sample-Report.pdf):
- 90/95/99 latency percentiles for 1K/5K/10K TPS test loads (sample).
- Token-level median latency and p95 for 8k token requests (30-day snapshot).
- Description of scheduled maintenance process and notification SLA (we propose 48 hours for planned maintenance; emergency maintenance will be notified ASAP with follow-up RCA).
- Lead-in steps for regional failover and expected RTO for cross-region failover (we can provide runbook excerpts).

Suggested order-form language (summary):
- Scoped carveout: during the initial 6-month migration period, Redwood will not be held to the standard availability target for scheduled maintenance windows up to 6 hours per month provided 48-hour notice is given.
- Telemetry delivery: Redwood will provide a monthly telemetry package during onboarding and weekly summaries for the first 60 days.
- Availability credits: proposed credit banding for partial-month availability below target (outlined in attached doc).

Attachments: SLA-Redlines-v1.docx, Telemetry-Sample-Report.pdf

If that looks ok, Laura and Kimberly can propose firm language to slot into your MSA/order-form.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Melissa Johnson <melissa.johnson@novacorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2025-07-20T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability carveout request + evidence for onboarding

Hi Melissa — looping in my suggested order-form KPIs and one-tab credit schedule (attached).

Quick notes after reviewing Ben's proposal:
- We can accept a 6-month scoped carveout with the proposed 48-hour notice for planned maintenance. We'll call this the "Migration Window" and reference it in the order form as an attachment (OrderForm-Availability-KPIs.xlsx).
- For telemetry, we'll provide: daily token-level latency histograms for the first 14 days, then weekly summaries through day 60, then monthly thereafter during the migration window. The format is a CSV export + a short interpretive summary.
- Credit schedule: instead of flat percentage credits, we propose a stepped banding tied to region impact and duration (see attached). This reduces negotiation friction with procurement teams used to banded credits.

Ben — I redlined a few sections in your SLA-Redlines-v1 so we can avoid unnecessary legal loops. Kimberly, if you agree with the credit mechanics I can update the Order Form workbook and send back for signature routing.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Melissa Johnson <melissa.johnson@novacorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2025-07-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability carveout request + evidence for onboarding

Melissa — attaching our final redline for the SLA rider and a Docusign route for the order form.

A few legal clarifications in plain language:
- We will include a defined "Migration Window" clause in the SOW that limits the carveout to scheduled maintenance with 48-hour notice and emergency maintenance which is limited to actions required to address critical security or data integrity incidents.
- Credits are remedial only and do not affect liability caps in the underlying MSA. Procurement should be aware credits are the exclusive remedy for availability shortfall during the Migration Window.
- For telemetry, we will provide a secure SharePoint/Drive link to the evidence package and a one-time snapshot of 30 days of historical telemetry once we sign. Ongoing weekly summaries will be pushed to the same link.

DocuSign and next steps: please review the attached Final-SLA-Rider-Redline.docx. If this is acceptable, Melissa, mark approvals in the Docusign link below and route to the procurement mailbox. We will turn around signature routing on our side within 24 hours of your execution.
